title: The general of the dhamma
hookLine: Sariputta, foremost in wisdom, who could explain what the Buddha said briefly

cards: A brahmin named Sela has just met the Buddha, and he is won over. He is also a practical man. A teacher this great, he reasons, must have someone at his side who carries the work forward, the way a king has a general.
So, in the Sutta Nipata, Sela asks it in verse: who is your general? Which disciple follows the teacher and keeps this going? It's a fair question about any movement.
Somebody has to explain the thing when the founder isn't in the room. The Buddha answers with one name.

teach.b: First, the name: Sariputta. In paraphrase, the Buddha tells Sela: the wheel of the teaching that I set rolling, Sariputta keeps rolling, the one who comes after me. That's where the picture of a general comes from.
Not a battle. A wheel that needs someone to keep it moving. Later tradition turned it into a title: the general of the dhamma.
Second, what he was known for.
In the Anguttara Nikaya's list of foremost disciples, the Buddha names Sariputta foremost in great wisdom.
And in the discourses his wisdom has a recognizable shape: the Buddha says something short, and Sariputta opens it up so others can use it. Third, one scene of that.
In the Samyutta Nikaya, a group of monks is about to leave for a far western country. The Buddha tells them: before you go, take leave of Sariputta. He's wise, and he helps his fellow monks.
So they go to him, and he gets them ready. Out there, he says, wise people will question you. They'll ask what your teacher teaches.
Answer simply: the removal of desire and lust. And if they ask, desire for what? Tell them: for the body, for feelings, for perceptions, for the rest of what we take ourselves to be.
One plain line first, then the next step only if someone asks for it. That is the general at work: not commanding, but equipping.
This week ran from Ashvaghosha himself, through honey, the poem closed, Upatissa, a pact and deathless, to today: the one who explains.

how: In Theravada communities Sariputta is honored as the chief disciple in wisdom, and his discourses in the Pali texts are studied as models of how to explain the teaching step by step.

games.q: you're one of the monks about to leave for a far country, where wise strangers will question you about your teacher. what do you do before you go?
o: leave right away and work it out on the road.
decide to say you're too new to answer.
go to Sariputta and let him prepare you.
games.why: the Buddha sends them to Sariputta, who readies them: answer first with one plain line, the removal of desire and lust, and go further only when asked.

practice: Pick something you understand well, how to make rice, what a word on this path means, and explain it silently the way Sariputta coached the travelers: one plain sentence, then stop.
Imagine someone asking what you mean, give only the next sentence, and come back to the breath.

wordCard.voice: Sariputta. The disciple the Buddha named, when Sela asked who kept the wheel of the teaching rolling, foremost in wisdom, who readied others to explain it simply.

orig.note: Pali: general (senapati) of the dhamma, a title later tradition gives Sariputta.

carryVoice: Your line: wisdom explains. One plain line first; the next only if someone asks. Day seven hundred twenty-eight, done.
